title: Port feedback-loop-diagnosis skill into opum-workflow
description: Source: opum-agent tooling/codex-skills/feedback-loop-diagnosis/SKILL.md, read-only from this side until the port ships (then delete there). Per OPAG-51's user-authorised port decision (2026-09-06, AskUserQuestion): port feedback-loop-diagnosis ONLY for now; tdd-seams and deep-module-design are decided later, gated on whether this port's baseline arm actually fails. decision-grilling is explicitly NOT ported (its own eval showed baseline unaided at 0.67 -- selection-by-cost-of-measurement mistake). Ship gate: ./scripts/run-eval.sh feedback-loop-diagnosis, 3 runs, --ablation with-without, sonnet-tier judge, one behavioural case whose baseline arm fails plus a no-trigger guard, authored against opum-agent docs/reference/plugin-eval-authoring.md -- read its three recorded grader defects (over-specified failure lists colliding with permission clauses) before writing the case so the criteria do not contain their own exception. Report the run result and cost back to opum-agent; the tdd-seams follow-on decision depends on it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: feedback-loop-diagnosis skill is ported into this plugin's skills/ with a behavioural eval case whose baseline arm fails
no-trigger guard case exists for the skill and passes (delta 0.00, both arms at parity)
./scripts/run-eval.sh feedback-loop-diagnosis passes at 3 runs with --ablation with-without and a sonnet-tier judge, or is recorded as evaluated-and-not-yet-passing with a diagnosed reason
run result and cost reported back to opum-agent to unblock the tdd-seams decision

implementationNotes: Ported skills/opum-feedback-loop-diagnosis/SKILL.md (rewritten, not translated: dropped the '$tdd-seams' macro load since tdd-seams is unshipped, and the 'active coordination plane' phrase, which named FMC without saying so, in favor of AskUserQuestion) plus skills/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md carrying the Matt Pocock MIT attribution this repo did not yet have.

Behavioural case: four design iterations, each empirically piloted (claude plugin eval --case ... --runs N), not guessed at. (1) feedback-loop-diagnosis-cache-key-collision, memoize bug with the exact colliding call sequence handed to the model in the ticket: both arms scored the diagnosis correctly via static reading alone in 1-2 turns; classic 'fixture contains the answer' defect (plugin-eval-authoring.md's own term). (2) Same file, vaguer symptom forcing the model to construct its own repro: judge variance dominated (with 0.33, without 1.00, delta -0.67 on n=1) on two near-identical high-quality responses -- an llm-only-scored case's known failure mode per the sdlc-promotion-mechanics precedent in the standards doc. (3) feedback-loop-diagnosis-unreproducible-failure, an epistemic-restraint framing (does the response decline to guess without evidence): n=1 showed delta 0.67 in the right direction, but n=3 collapsed to delta 0.00 (with 0.78, without 0.78) -- the n=1 result was noise. (4) feedback-loop-diagnosis-stale-fix-claim, a scaffolded 3-file investigation (tracker task claiming a fix, a captured incident log, and source whose retry guard doesn't actually cover the logged error) closely modeled on handoff-write-mechanics' shape: n=3 gives with 1.00/1.00/1.00, without 1.00/1.00/1.00, delta 0.000 exactly, $1.20. Kept as the shipped case despite the flat delta because it is the best-designed of the four and documents the finding precisely.

Root cause, not a grader defect: the Skill tool was invoked 0 times across every with-arm run in all four case designs (turn counts 1-6, well under the 15-25 budget granted). Sonnet-tier baseline evidently doesn't need explicit skill guidance to perform this style of textual/investigative debugging correctly, unlike opum-sdlc/opum-handoff's cases, which encode this fleet's own proprietary process (task IDs, branch conventions, the trust order) a base model cannot know without the skill. A general debugging methodology overlaps too heavily with what a strong model already does by default to produce a measurable with/without delta in a plan-graded (no-Bash) eval. Did not attempt a Bash-granted execution case: --allow-tools is an operator-level grant run-eval.sh deliberately never passes (every existing case in this plugin is plan-graded for the same reason), and widening that felt like a bigger infra decision than this task's scope, not something to do unilaterally mid-port.

Canonical gate: ./scripts/run-eval.sh feedback-loop-diagnosis exits 0 ($4.36 total across both invocations: the skill's-own-cases run plus the all-skills no-trigger-guard run, with feedback-loop-diagnosis-no-trigger-test-runner-choice counted in both by the script's own design). Both cases score 1.00 in both arms -- the script's threshold check (nothing below 1.0) passes, and adding this skill caused zero regression to handoff-no-trigger-session-state or sdlc-no-trigger-unrelated. But 'the script exits 0' is not the same claim as 'the skill demonstrably helps': that requires delta > 0, i.e. baseline scoring BELOW 1.0 while the with-arm holds 1.0, which is exactly acceptance criterion 0's bar and exactly what four iterations did not produce. Checking criterion 2 as met on the literal text (the script does pass at 3 runs); leaving criterion 0 unchecked, since it is not met and conflating the two would misrepresent what was actually shown.
